facts.text: Around 1900, Jewish immigrant brothers Adolph, Isaac, Sidney, and Lee Felsenthal founded the town, becoming the area's first Jewish settlers.
On July 6, 1904, Felsenthal was officially incorporated, marking its transition from speculative land holding to a structured municipality.
Felsenthal sits just outside the 65,000‑acre Felsenthal National Wildlife Refuge, a protected area established in 1975.
Adolph Felsenthal bought 1,200 acres near the Ouachita‑Saline confluence, anticipating a river‑rail junction that would be the only such point between Camden and Monroe.
In 1904, the Felsenthal Brick Company began using local clay deposits to manufacture bricks, fueling the town's early industrial growth.
The town hosts an annual Breamfest fishing tournament and rib cookoff, drawing outdoor enthusiasts to its riverfront.
